title: Chunks that don't overlap
hints: items[i:j] shares memory with items, and its capacity runs to the end of items. So appending to that sub-slice overwrites items[j] in place.
A full slice expression items[i:j:j] caps the capacity at j-i, which makes append allocate a new array instead. Copying each chunk works too.
for start := 0; start < len(items); start += size { end := min(start+size, len(items)); chunks = append(chunks, items[start:end:end]) }. Return nil if size <= 0.
